status_summary: Per capita caps, aggregate caps and block grants were not found in the enacted law or in the CMS rules implementing it. Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) instead includes provider tax limits (sections 71115 and 71117), state directed payment limits (section 71116) and the end of a temporary expansion FMAP incentive (section 71114). As described in CMS's rulemaking, section 71115 replaces the 6 percent indirect hold-harmless threshold with each class's level as of 2025-07-04 for fiscal years beginning on or after 2026-10-01, and for expansion states phases that threshold down from 5.5 percent in federal fiscal year 2028 by half a point a year to 3.5 percent in fiscal year 2032 (nursing facility and ICF/IID classes are not phased down); section 71116 limits total state directed payment rates for inpatient hospital, outpatient hospital, nursing facility and academic medical center practitioner services to 100 percent of Medicare rates in expansion states and 110 percent in non-expansion states, for rating periods beginning on or after 2025-07-04, with grandfathered payments phased down from the first rating period on or after 2028-01-01. CMS finalized a rule on 2026-02-02 (effective 2026-04-03) closing a health care-related tax loophole and codifying section 71117 (proposed 2025-05-15), proposed on 2026-05-22 (91 FR 30400; comments closed 2026-07-21) to implement the directed payment limits and to extend a payment limit to all directed payments and certain fee-for-service targeted practitioner payments, and proposed on 2026-07-23 (91 FR 46562; comments closed 2026-09-21) a rule on the indirect hold-harmless threshold implementing the statute, with a proposed 6 percent ceiling on any threshold. Reform of disproportionate share hospital payments was not found.

timeline.event: CMS proposes a rule to close a health care-related tax loophole, so that taxes set higher for Medicaid business than for other business cannot qualify for tax waivers unless generally redistributive.

Public Law 119-21 is signed, with Medicaid sections on provider taxes (71115, 71117), state directed payments (71116), the expansion FMAP incentive (71114) and budget neutrality for section 1115 demonstrations (71118); the provider tax and directed payment limits are described in CMS's 2026 proposed rules, which cite the statute.
CMS finalizes the health care-related tax loophole rule and implements newer statutory requirements for generally redistributive taxes.

CMS proposes (91 FR 30400, comments through 2026-07-21) to implement the statutory limits on state directed payments (100 percent of Medicare rates in expansion states and 110 percent in non-expansion states for inpatient, outpatient, nursing facility and academic medical center practitioner services, with grandfathered payments phased down from 2028-01-01), and goes beyond the statute by proposing alternatives for a payment limit on all directed payments, all states and territories, and a limit on certain targeted practitioner payments in fee-for-service.

CMS proposes (91 FR 46562, CMS-2452-P, comments through 2026-09-21) standards for indirect hold-harmless arrangements implementing section 71115: from fiscal years beginning on or after 2026-10-01 each class's threshold is its 2025-07-04 level (0 percent if no tax existed), and for expansion states it phases down from 5.5 percent in federal fiscal year 2028 to 3.5 percent in 2032; CMS also proposes a 6 percent ceiling on any threshold.
